conclusion: First promotion-role cycle in this lineage. Root-caused (not just observed): stage_wall_minutes_for_role() clamps both screening and promotion roles to the same MAX_RUN_MINUTES=3 ceiling, and the per-experiment wall budget (~46.7s, campaign budget.max_wall_minutes=0.7778) is split between train+eval without accounting for eval_suites_for_role() needing 2 suites/8 records for promotion versus 1 suite/3 records for screening. Training itself was fast (3.24s / 8.42s), so the eval stage's fair-share decode timeout (_effective_record_decode_timeout in eval_runner.py) collapsed to ~2.7-3.4s per record -- too tight for this CPU sandbox's decode latency, especially with the component-plan arm's extra head. This mirrors several historical incidents in this loop family (autotrain-cycle-1715/1716/1717/1737 in docs/MODEL_CARD.md) where CPU-sandbox decode timing conflicts with the fixed wall cap. A real fix would need to re-balance execute_commands' train/eval wall-time split by role in src/slm_training/autoresearch/engine.py, which has exact-value timing tests (test_execute_shares_one_wall_budget_across_stages, test_execute_passes_inner_wall_to_evaluation) and has seen ~10 recent dedicated PRs on this exact class of problem -- not something to patch speculatively in one pass without deeper context. Deferred rather than risked.
next_priorities: Re-balance execute_commands' per-stage wall-time split by cycle_role/eval_suites_for_role() count so promotion cycles get a suite-count-aware eval floor, not just leftover-after-training (owner: improve-openui-harnesses, harness_family: model_build)
Until that lands, expect promotion-role cycles to keep hitting decode_timeout on this CPU sandbox; frozen replay of c4-control/c4-component-plan is the only reuse path
Do not promote or ship either checkpoint
